vocabulary.definition: The installable Python CLI artifact, distinct from a target repository.
The repository selected by an operator as the installation destination.
A file whose path, version, and content ownership are declared by the installer manifest.
Any target file not proven managed by the same installer version.

relationships.relationship: One distribution package applies one versioned manifest to zero or more target repositories; a target has many files, each classified as managed, target-owned, or unresolved.

invariants: The target must be an existing Git worktree whose resolved root is validated before any future mutation.
The installer must not copy credentials, tasks, planning artifacts, .harness runtime runs, caches, Git history, or target task data.
A target-owned or modified managed file must not be overwritten without an explicit approved collision action.
Dry-run must not modify the target repository.
Target-controlled ownership state is untrusted until its schema, manifest identity, exact path set, and provenance are validated.
Apply requires exclusive target coordination, no-follow path handling, staged writes, and rollback evidence before implementation can be approved.
